misconceptions.description: Jumping from a single classroom moment straight to a verdict about a student without describing what was actually observed
misconceptions.trigger: teacher records "Jordan is unmotivated" instead of the specific observable behavior in the moment
misconceptions.feedback: Separate what you saw from what it means. Describe the observable first; the interpretation and the revision come after.

misconceptions.description: Overhauling a lesson based on one student's reaction or one confusing moment, ignoring the rest of the evidence
misconceptions.trigger: teacher rewrites the whole plan because one student looked lost
misconceptions.feedback: Weigh the moment against the pattern. One signal warrants a check, not a redesign; look for whether it recurs.

misconceptions.description: Recording that a lesson was changed without naming the noticed evidence that prompted the change
misconceptions.trigger: revision note says what changed but not what was noticed that justified it
misconceptions.feedback: Link every revision to the moment you noticed. A change with no triggering observation is not yet evidence-based.
